proposition: The New York City Council constituent-services hackathon took place on January 30, 2016.
publicWording: The event took place on January 30, 2016.

proposition: Civic Hall announced the January 30 event for 1–3 p.m.
publicWording: Civic Hall announced the session for 1–3 p.m.
antiClaims: Independent evidence proves the event began at 1 p.m. and ended at 3 p.m.
2:10 p.m. was the event start time.
qualifications: The time window comes from Civic Hall's announcement.

proposition: The January 30, 2016 CouncilStat hackathon took place at Civic Hall.
publicWording: The Council convened the event at Civic Hall.
antiClaims: The event occurred at an inherited NoMad map pin.

proposition: The January 2016 hackathon previewed CouncilStat constituent-services data and explored how to improve constituent services and data usability.
publicWording: Participants previewed CouncilStat constituent-services data and explored how it could become more usable and transparent.
qualifications: The Council's retrospective public post is the source for the preview and improvement purpose.

proposition: The New York City Council described the gathering as its first CouncilStat hackathon.
publicWording: The Council described it that day as its first CouncilStat hackathon.
antiClaims: It was definitively New York City's first civic-data hackathon.
It was the first municipal hackathon of any kind.

proposition: A recovered promotional graphic used the wording “New York City Council Hackathon” and displayed labs.council.nyc.
publicWording: A Council-branded graphic used the wording “New York City Council Hackathon.”
antiClaims: “New York City Council Hackathon” is proven to be the complete formal registration title.
qualifications: Treat the wording as recovered promotional branding only.

proposition: A participant photograph documents a “Digital District — Help improve City Council District office operations” breakout placard at approximately 2:10 p.m.
antiClaims: “Digital District” was the official event title.
2:10 p.m. was the event start time.
Jamie facilitated the Digital District breakout.
qualifications: Do not project publicly until photographer credit and rights review are complete.

proposition: No dedicated Civic Hall calendar listing or event-detail page was recovered in the current research pass.
publicWording: No dedicated Civic Hall event page has been recovered.
antiClaims: Civic Hall never published an event page.
A dedicated Civic Hall event listing was proven not to exist.
qualifications: A negative search result is bounded by the search method and surviving archive.

proposition: No complete agenda, participant roster, breakout roster, or registration form was recovered in the current research pass.
antiClaims: A complete agenda, roster, or registration form was recovered.
Melissa Mark-Viverito is confirmed as an attendee.
qualifications: The surviving posts and graphic do not establish a full agenda or roster.
Failure to recover these records does not prove that they never existed.

proposition: Jamie independently built CallNYC.org after the full CouncilStat constituent-services data became public.
publicWording: After the complete dataset became public, Jamie independently built CallNYC.org as a resident-facing interpretation of the records.
antiClaims: CallNYC was built during the hackathon.
CallNYC was a formal hackathon submission.
CallNYC was an official Council product.
CallNYC was adopted by the Council.
qualifications: Do not state a precise data-release day; the public record supports March 2016 and a release before the March 14 Politico article.

proposition: CouncilStat case counts were not a uniform performance measure because district offices used and updated the system differently and recorded work with different frequency.
publicWording: Different Council offices used CouncilStat differently and entered information with different frequency, so recorded case counts could not safely be read as a simple office-quality measure.
antiClaims: CouncilStat case counts directly measured office quality.
A larger recorded caseload proved greater resident need or office effectiveness.
qualifications: Politico reported staff cautions about different usage and entry frequency across offices.
Jamie also noted that more district-office work occurred than the dataset reflected.

proposition: Politico New York covered CallNYC on March 14, 2016.
publicWording: Politico New York covered CallNYC on March 14, 2016.

proposition: A public GitHub repository preserves CallNYC project code.
publicWording: The public repository preserves the project code.
antiClaims: Repository existence proves official Council adoption or current service status.
